newsitem.title: UK: Sean Connery urges Scots to vote for nationalists.
newsitem.headline: Sean Connery urges Scots to vote for nationalists.

text.p: Scottish film star Sean Connery strode onto Britain's election stage on Wednesday with a letter urging his countrymen to back the campaign for an independent Scotland by voting for the Scottish National Party (SNP).

"I am proud to come from Scotland and my dearest wish is to see Scotland free," wrote the 66-year-old Oscar-winning actor, who has played James Bond, Indiana Jones' father and English hero King Arthur among other film roles.

The SNP, which holds four seats in Britain's parliament and hopes to increase this tally in the May 1 election, said it was mailing the letter to hundreds of thousands of Scots, targeting wavering voters and marginal seats.

The party wants full independence for Scotland. Recent opinion polls give it support of around 21 percent in Scotland, second only to Britain's main opposition Labour Party which has support of about 47 percent in Scotland.

"I have supported the SNP for many years because I know that every vote for the SNP is a vote that puts Scotland back on the map and forces London to sit up and take notice," Connery said in his letter.

"Everywhere I go in the world people want to know about Scotland and why we tolerate our affairs being run by someone else's government," he said. "If the SNP wins, so does Scotland -- it's as simple as that."
Connery has helped the SNP before -- he spoke on a television broadcast by the party in November. The SNP said the broadcast gave a major boost to the party's membership numbers.
Scotland is part of the United Kingdom which also comprises England, Wales and Northern Ireland. It has been governed by London since 1707 but retains its own legal and education systems.
